key_insight: HaRP improves high dynamic range capture in rolling-shutter mobile cameras by combining two complementary scans: standard RSGR and an inverted reversed scan. This dual-view setup helps recover more scene detail while reducing motion-related capture limitations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses rolling-shutter distortions and the limited speed and dynamic range of rolling shutter with global reset (RSGR) imaging in CMOS mobile photography.
method: Use a dual reversed shutter scanning setup that captures both RSGR and inverted RSGR views of the scene.
Fuse the complementary views to better preserve dynamic range and reduce artifacts from motion and scan timing.
Leverage the opposing scan directions to compensate for the limitations of a single shutter configuration.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical sensor-level strategy for improving mobile image quality under motion and lighting extremes. It can enable more robust downstream vision tasks by producing cleaner, more information-rich captures.

paper_title: HaRP: High Dynamic Range Photosequencing through Dual Reversed Shutter Scanning
